meta.title: Después: el Monumental está donde estaba el MUT
meta.question: ¿Qué pasaría si intercambiamos de lugar el MUT y el Estadio Monumental de Colo-Colo?
meta.analyze: Cómo llega la misma hinchada a cada estadio y cuánto demora el viaje.

cues.caption: Movimos el Monumental a Tobalaba, donde estaba el MUT.
Ahora 27.790 hinchas llegan en transporte público. En Macul eran 23.688.
En auto llegan 9.398 hinchas. En Macul eran 12.759.
El viaje en transporte público dura 59,0 minutos en promedio. En Macul, 54,8.
El estadio es más grande que el MUT y ocupa 6 tramos de calle, que se cierran.
El MUT ya no está: al Metro Tobalaba entran 2.599 personas menos al día.
El MUT se muda a Macul, al sitio del estadio, y lleva 4.626 empleos.
Por esos empleos, al Metro Pedrero entran 2.250 personas más al día.
Y al Metro Mirador entran 1.827 personas más al día.
Con el estadio en Tobalaba, 3.361 hinchas menos llegan en auto al partido.

assumptions: Persons are synthetic and consistent with the Census 2024 margins. They are not microdata.
The station model (L9) is fitted on the baseline. Its scale, classes and profiles do not change.
Travel times are comuna to comuna and lower than survey times. The effect of a time change is an unvalidated sensitivity; the size and direction of its error are unknown.
Stations use the baseline public share of the home comuna, scaled by the change in its public-transport workers.
Open city for residents: more or fewer residents change the total of workers, with the baseline workers per resident of the comuna.
Station access (L9): a walk within 1,000 m, or else one bus. A closed station does not change the travel minutes between comunas or the job choice.
Students do not choose again.
Trips are display groups of workers, not persons. Departure half hours come from the EOD 2012 survey. Students are not included.

The Census sets walking and cycling totals inside each comuna pair. The 2012 survey distance rule allocates workers within those totals. The engine has no measured response for cycling uptake after a new cycleway.
All values are model values, not measured values.
Attendance and the end half hour are scenario inputs. Unmodeled attendance has no assigned origin.
A supplied origin profile gives origins only. Mode, return destination, and Metro demand are unestimated. The separate Colo-Colo fan_base has its own modeled origins and modes.

When a mode loses places, who keeps it is a deterministic weighted draw: the weight is the Census 2024 share of that mode among workers of the same home comuna, age band and household size. Unknown household size has its own group for the draw. These workers count in age summaries only. mode_change_by_person follows from this rule, not from an observed response. Workers that a residents change adds are not counted.

Known stocks use uniform density over the footprint's covered census-block area. Shares sum to one across covered area; street gaps receive no stock. Scalar block metadata and any occupancy rate use the largest-area block.

A supplied origin profile gives origins only. Mode, return destination, and Metro demand are unestimated. The separate Colo-Colo fan_base has its own modeled origins and modes.

Fan base: a comuna sends attendees in proportion to population × Colo-Colo share. The share mixes Cadem 2024 support by group (C1 24%, C2 38%, C3 39%, D/E 49%) with the education of Census 2024 household heads as the group proxy (fan_base.csv).
The same fans go to the match at any venue; the attendance does not fall with travel time.
Mode to the match = the commute mode shares of the pair home comuna → venue comuna (Census 2024 calibration). Weekend service and parking at the venue are not modeled.

optional_visits.unit: persons who make an optional weekday shopping visit (workers and other residents); trips = persons × 1.608 (EOD 2012 trips per shopper)

population.source: workers: Census 2024 internal commuters (mode_od.csv); students: MINEDUC 2026 enrollment (school_od.csv); other_residents: Census 2024 persons who are neither an internal commuter nor attend basic or secondary school (Census attendance, person_traits_residents.csv). The MINEDUC student count and the Census exclusion cover different school levels, and a commuting student can count as both a worker and a student, so the three groups can overlap. Other residents have a home and traits; their only modeled trip is the optional shopping visit (optional_visits).

shopping.unit: weekday outbound shopping trips of residents (EOD 2012 rates × Census 2024 residents), not distinct persons; returns are not included
